{
  "IP": "neorv32_cpu_icc",
  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "CSR access command",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cpu_icc",
      "Information": "The command specifying whether a CSR read or write occurs and which ICC data or status register is targeted controls access to the transmit queue and receive-side readback. It is received through the CSR access ports and does not leave the unit as a carried value.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The command is sensitive control information, and the RTL decodes csr_re_i and csr_addr_i into the transmit acknowledgement while csr_we_i and csr_addr_i directly generate the FIFO write decision at lines 59-60, so tampering can change which accesses occur. The command gates both the transmit write path and the acknowledgement of a CSR read, so suppressing or altering it can block required transfers at lines 59-60.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could forge, suppress, or retarget the CSR strobes and address so that transmit data is written incorrectly or receive and transmit transfers are prevented.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "csr_we_i",
        "csr_re_i",
        "csr_addr_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [
        46,
        47,
        59,
        60
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        46,
        47,
        59,
        60
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    }
  ],
  "Not Kept": [
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Transmitted ICC data",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_icc",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The transmit data only moves from csr_wdata_i through the FIFO instance to icc_tx_o.dat at lines 81 and 86, so Forwarded transactions and the FIFO-buffer rules exclude it as information of this unit."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Received ICC data",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_icc",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The receive data is only copied from icc_rx_i.dat to the CSR readback at line 52 without being stored or computed by this unit, so the Forwarded transactions and Transfer records rules bar it as a separate piece."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "ICC transfer handshake",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_icc",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The ack, ready, and receive acknowledgement fields only time or qualify ICC transfers at lines 59, 85, and 87, so Transfer records and FIFO-buffer rules do not keep them as independent information."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Transmit FIFO availability status",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_icc",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "tx_fifo_free and icc_tx_o.rdy only report or gate movement through the FIFO at lines 49, 83, and 87, which the Buffer and engine status bits and Port buffers rules exclude as a piece of its own."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Clock and reset timing",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_icc",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The clock and reset are only wired to the FIFO instance at lines 75-76 and are excluded from conceptual assets by the Clocks and resets rule."
    }
  ],
  "Notes": []
}

conceptual assets.information: The command specifying whether a CSR read or write occurs and which ICC data or status register is targeted controls access to the transmit queue and receive-side readback. It is received through the CSR access ports and does not leave the unit as a carried value.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The command is sensitive control information, and the RTL decodes csr_re_i and csr_addr_i into the transmit acknowledgement while csr_we_i and csr_addr_i directly generate the FIFO write decision at lines 59-60, so tampering can change which accesses occur. The command gates both the transmit write path and the acknowledgement of a CSR read, so suppressing or altering it can block required transfers at lines 59-60.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could forge, suppress, or retarget the CSR strobes and address so that transmit data is written incorrectly or receive and transmit transfers are prevented.

considered, not kept.reason: The transmit data only moves from csr_wdata_i through the FIFO instance to icc_tx_o.dat at lines 81 and 86, so Forwarded transactions and the FIFO-buffer rules exclude it as information of this unit.

The receive data is only copied from icc_rx_i.dat to the CSR readback at line 52 without being stored or computed by this unit, so the Forwarded transactions and Transfer records rules bar it as a separate piece.
The ack, ready, and receive acknowledgement fields only time or qualify ICC transfers at lines 59, 85, and 87, so Transfer records and FIFO-buffer rules do not keep them as independent information.
tx_fifo_free and icc_tx_o.rdy only report or gate movement through the FIFO at lines 49, 83, and 87, which the Buffer and engine status bits and Port buffers rules exclude as a piece of its own.
The clock and reset are only wired to the FIFO instance at lines 75-76 and are excluded from conceptual assets by the Clocks and resets rule.
